# Retrieval context — Scubiee host MCP permission/allowlist grant flow

## Problem restatement (≤8 lines)
Trace, end-to-end, how Scubiee grants host MCP tool permissions during
`connect`/install: (1) where the "locate" tool-name allowlist is defined,
(2) how an `mcpServers.scubiee` entry gets `autoApprove`/`alwaysAllow` (or
equivalent) baked in, (3) how project-level permission surfaces (Cursor
`permissions.json` `mcpAllowlist`, Claude `settings.json` `permissions.allow`,
Continue's yaml template, docs-only stubs) are merged/written, (4) how
`write_project_tool_surface` ties `mcp.json` + these permission artifacts
together across hosts, and (5) how a `"locate"` profile differs from an
`"all"` profile.

## Ordered call/flow narrative

1. **Entry point (per-tool, per-repo):** `write_project_tool_surface(repo, tool, dry_run=...)`
   in `rules_installer.py` is the top of the install/connect path for one
   connected host `tool: ToolDef`. It does three things in order:
   a. `_write_workspace_mcp(tool, root)` → writes the host's `mcp.json`
      (or equivalent) file(s), returning the paths written.
   b. `write_project_gate_rules(root, slugs=[tool.slug])` → writes the
      steering/AGENTS.md GATE rules (unrelated to permissions, but part of
      "tool surface").
   c. `apply_permissions_to_repo_tool_surface(tool.slug, root, dry_run=...)`
      (imported from `mcp_permissions.py`) → writes the host-specific
      permission sidecar/allowlist artifacts. This is the step that answers
      most of the question.
   `dry_run=True` mirrors the same three calls but only reports
   `would_write_*` without touching disk.

2. **Building the mcp.json entry itself:** `_write_workspace_mcp` (not fully
   expanded here, but it is the writer that calls `format_server_entry`)
   ultimately produces the JSON block per host schema via
   `format_server_entry(tool, repo, pin_repo, schema)` in `rules_installer.py`.
   This function:
   - builds `command`/`args`/`env` from `server_entry(...)`,
   - branches on `tool.mcp_schema` (`claude`, `vscode`, `copilot_cli`,
     `opencode`, `amp`, `codex`, `continue`, `zed`) to shape the entry to
     that host's expected JSON fields,
   - then at the very end calls
     `enrich_server_entry_permissions(entry, tool.slug)` from
     `mcp_permissions.py` before returning — **this is where
     autoApprove/alwaysAllow get injected directly into the mcpServers
     entry**, before it's ever written to disk.

3. **Defining which tools are allowed ("locate" tool list):**
   `mcp_permissions.py::PHASE_LOCATE_TOOLS` is the canonical ship allowlist:
   `("gate", "map", "pack_context", "expand_context", "collect_hot_context",
   "workspace", "expand", "status")`. There are also
   `PHASE_LAB_LOCATE_TOOLS`, `PHASE_CLASSIC_LOCATE_TOOLS` (opt-in via
   `CTX_MCP_EXPERIMENT=lab|classic`), and `LEGACY_LOCATE_TOOLS` (rich
   surfaces like `search`, `files`, `read`, `recall`, `neighbors`, `graph`,
   `outline`).
   `locate_tool_names(profile="locate"|"all")` returns
   `PHASE_LOCATE_TOOLS` for `"locate"`, or
   `PHASE_LOCATE_TOOLS + LEGACY_LOCATE_TOOLS` for `"all"`.

4. **Enriching the mcpServers entry:**
   `enrich_server_entry_permissions(entry, tool_slug, profile="locate")`:
   - Looks up `tool_permission_plan(tool_slug)` → a `ToolPermissionPlan`
     (`mechanism`, `sidecar_paths`, `notes`) from the `_TOOL_PLANS` dict.
   - If `mechanism` is `"already_builtin"` or `"docs_only"`, returns the
     entry unchanged (Copilot CLI already ships `tools:["*"]`; Codex/Zed/Amp
     have no embeddable field).
   - If `mechanism == "embedded_mcp"` (or `tool_slug` is in
     `_EMBEDDED_MCP_SLUGS` — includes **`kiro`**, `cline`, `roo-code`,
     `cursor`, `devin-desktop`, `pi`, `claude-code`):
     - clears any sticky `disabled: True` (special-cased: for `cursor` it
       pops the key; for everyone else in this branch it force-sets
       `disabled = False`),
     - flips `enabled` back to `True` if it was `False`,
     - sets `entry["autoApprove"] = locate_tool_names(profile)` (or `["*"]`
       for profile `"all"`),
     - sets `entry["alwaysAllow"]` to the same list.
   - If `tool_slug == "opencode"`, sets `autoApprove` similarly plus
     `enabled = True`.
   - Otherwise returns entry unchanged.
   This is the **direct embedded autoApprove/alwaysAllow mechanism** used by
   Cline/Roo/Cursor/Kiro/Devin/Pi/Claude Code/OpenCode server blocks.

5. **Cross-host permission "plans" table:** `_TOOL_PLANS: dict[str, ToolPermissionPlan]`
   in `mcp_permissions.py` maps slug → mechanism:
   - `cursor` → `sidecar_json`, path `.cursor/permissions.json` (Run Mode
     `mcpAllowlist` **plus** embedded autoApprove — belongs to both
     `_EMBEDDED_MCP_SLUGS` and has a sidecar plan; `enrich_server_entry_permissions`
     still special-cases `cursor` to `pop("disabled")` instead of forcing
     `False`).
   - `claude-code` → `sidecar_json`, path `.claude/settings.json`.
   - `codex` → `docs_only`, `.codex/SCUBIEE_MCP_PERMISSIONS.md`.
   - `copilot` → `already_builtin` (VS Code UI or `tools:["*"]`).
   - `continue` → `sidecar_yaml`, `.continue/scubiee-permissions.yaml` +
     `.continue/SCUBIEE_MCP_PERMISSIONS.md`.
   - `opencode` → `embedded_mcp`.
   - `zed` → `docs_only`, `.zed/SCUBIEE_MCP_PERMISSIONS.md`.
   - `amp` → `docs_only`, `.amp/SCUBIEE_MCP_PERMISSIONS.md`.
   - Loop at module load: `for _slug in _EMBEDDED_MCP_SLUGS:
     _TOOL_PLANS.setdefault(_slug, ToolPermissionPlan(mechanism="embedded_mcp", ...))`
     — this is what gives **`kiro`** (and `cline`, `roo-code`, `devin-desktop`,
     `pi`) their plan: pure embedded `autoApprove + alwaysAllow` on the
     `mcpServers.scubiee` entry, **no sidecar file at all**. So for Kiro the
     entire permission grant happens in step 4 (embedding), and
     `write_tool_permission_artifacts` short-circuits with
     `skipped=True, skip_reason="embedded on mcpServers entry during connect"`.

6. **Sidecar/project-level permission-surface writer:**
   `apply_permissions_to_repo_tool_surface(tool_slug, repo, profile, dry_run)`
   is a thin wrapper that calls `write_tool_permission_artifacts(...)`
   (same module). That function:
   - looks up the plan again; returns early (`skipped`) for `unknown tool`
     or `already_builtin`;
   - reads `CTX_MCP_PERMISSIONS_USER` env var to decide whether to also
     write a user-home copy (`include_user_home`);
   - branches on `tool_slug`:
     - **`cursor`**: `merge_cursor_permissions(root/".cursor/permissions.json", profile=...)`
       (project) and optionally `Path.home()/".cursor/permissions.json"` (user).
     - **`claude-code`**: `merge_claude_settings_permissions(root/".claude/settings.json", profile=...)`
       (project + optional user copy).
     - **`continue`**: writes `.continue/scubiee-permissions.yaml`
       (from `_continue_permissions_yaml`) + a README stub, via
       `atomic_write_text` (from `artifact_guard.py`).
     - **`codex` / `zed` / `amp`** (`docs_only`): writes a single markdown
       stub `SCUBIEE_MCP_PERMISSIONS.md` via `_permissions_readme(...)`.
     - **`embedded_mcp` plans** (e.g. Kiro, Cline, Roo, Cursor's embedded
       half, OpenCode): `report["skipped"] = True`,
       `report["skip_reason"] = "embedded on mcpServers entry during connect"`
       — nothing else to write; the grant already happened via
       `enrich_server_entry_permissions` in step 4.
   - Regardless of branch, always finishes by calling
     `_write_permissions_manifest(root, tool_slug, report, dry_run)`.

7. **Merge logic for the two concrete sidecar JSON formats:**
   - `merge_cursor_permissions(path, profile)`:
     - loads existing `.cursor/permissions.json` via `_load_json_object`
       (returns `{}` on missing/corrupt file — silently tolerant, unlike the
       mcp.json merge path which raises on corrupt JSON),
     - computes `additions = _cursor_mcp_allowlist(profile)` →
       for `profile="all"`: `["scubiee:*", "*:*"]`;
       for `profile="locate"`: `["scubiee:*"] + [f"*:{tool}" for tool in PHASE_LOCATE_TOOLS]`
       (the `*:{tool}` wildcards guard against Cursor renaming/prefixing the
       server namespace),
     - prunes stale classic/lab tool entries via
       `_prune_stale_scubiee_allowlist_entries` (drops leftover
       `*:focus`/`*:grep`/etc. from older connects when profile is `"locate"`),
     - merges into `document["mcpAllowlist"]` via `_merge_unique_strings`
       (order-preserving de-dup),
     - also rewrites `document["autoRun"]["allow_instructions"]`: strips any
       older "focus, grep, glob" coaching line and appends a fresh
       "Allow Scubiee MCP locate tools (gate, map, pack_context, ...)" line,
     - writes atomically via `_write_json_object` → `atomic_write_text`,
       `json.dumps(..., indent=2, sort_keys=True)`.
   - `merge_claude_settings_permissions(path, profile)`:
     - loads `.claude/settings.json`, sets `$schema` if absent,
     - reads/creates `document["permissions"]["allow"]` list,
     - prunes stale entries (same helper),
     - merges in `_claude_allow_rules(profile)` →
       for `"all"`: `["mcp__scubiee__*"]`;
       for `"locate"`: `[f"mcp__scubiee__{tool}" for tool in PHASE_LOCATE_TOOLS] + ["mcp__scubiee__*"]`
       (note: locate profile *also* appends the wildcard at the end —
       both explicit tool names and a trailing wildcard are present),
     - writes back via `_write_json_object`.

8. **Manifest / bookkeeping:** `_write_permissions_manifest(root, tool_slug, report, dry_run)`
   writes `.scubiee/mcp-permissions.json`, merging per-tool state:
   `{"tools": {slug: {"profile", "plan": ToolPermissionPlan.__dict__, "artifacts", "skipped"}}, "server": MCP_SERVER_NAME, "locate_tools": locate_tool_names()}`.
   This is a local audit trail, not something a host reads for approvals.

9. **mcp.json write-and-verify (the counterpart to permissions):**
   `_write_workspace_mcp` → `_write_mcp_json_keyed(path, key, entry)` merges
   the enriched `entry` (already containing autoApprove/alwaysAllow from
   step 4) into the correct top-level key (`mcpServers`, `servers`, `mcp`,
   or `amp.mcpServers` depending on host) under `_SERVER_NAME`, using
   `_load_json_for_merge` (raises `MCPConfigMergeError` on corrupt JSON or
   non-object root — stricter than the tolerant `_load_json_object` used for
   permission sidecars) and `strip_legacy_mcp_keys` (from `branding.py`) to
   remove old server aliases before re-inserting. After writing,
   `write_project_tool_surface` calls `mcp_install.py::verify_mcp_json(mcp_path)`
   on every written `.json` path and records failures into
   `report["mcp_verify"]`, flipping `report["ok"] = False` if any fail.

# Retrieval context — Scubiee host MCP permission/allowlist grant flow

## Problem restatement (≤8 lines)
Trace, end-to-end, how Scubiee grants host MCP tool permissions during
`connect`/install: (1) where the "locate" tool-name allowlist is defined,
(2) how an `mcpServers.scubiee` entry gets `autoApprove`/`alwaysAllow` (or
equivalent) baked in, (3) how project-level permission surfaces (Cursor
`permissions.json` `mcpAllowlist`, Claude `settings.json` `permissions.allow`,
Continue's yaml template, docs-only stubs) are merged/written, (4) how
`write_project_tool_surface` ties `mcp.json` + these permission artifacts
together across hosts, and (5) how a `"locate"` profile differs from an
`"all"` profile.

## Ordered call/flow narrative

1. **Entry point (per-tool, per-repo):** `write_project_tool_surface(repo, tool, dry_run=...)`
   in `rules_installer.py` is the top of the install/connect path for one
   connected host `tool: ToolDef`. It does three things in order:
   a. `_write_workspace_mcp(tool, root)` → writes the host's `mcp.json`
      (or equivalent) file(s), returning the paths written.
   b. `write_project_gate_rules(root, slugs=[tool.slug])` → writes the
      steering/AGENTS.md GATE rules (unrelated to permissions, but part of
      "tool surface").
   c. `apply_permissions_to_repo_tool_surface(tool.slug, root, dry_run=...)`
      (imported from `mcp_permissions.py`) → writes the host-specific
      permission sidecar/allowlist artifacts. This is the step that answers
      most of the question.
   `dry_run=True` mirrors the same three calls but only reports
   `would_write_*` without touching disk.

2. **Building the mcp.json entry itself:** `_write_workspace_mcp` (not fully
   expanded here, but it is the writer that calls `format_server_entry`)
   ultimately produces the JSON block per host schema via
   `format_server_entry(tool, repo, pin_repo, schema)` in `rules_installer.py`.
   This function:
   - builds `command`/`args`/`env` from `server_entry(...)`,
   - branches on `tool.mcp_schema` (`claude`, `vscode`, `copilot_cli`,
     `opencode`, `amp`, `codex`, `continue`, `zed`) to shape the entry to
     that host's expected JSON fields,
   - then at the very end calls
     `enrich_server_entry_permissions(entry, tool.slug)` from
     `mcp_permissions.py` before returning — **this is where
     autoApprove/alwaysAllow get injected directly into the mcpServers
     entry**, before it's ever written to disk.

3. **Defining which tools are allowed ("locate" tool list):**
   `mcp_permissions.py::PHASE_LOCATE_TOOLS` is the canonical ship allowlist:
   `("gate", "map", "pack_context", "expand_context", "collect_hot_context",
   "workspace", "expand", "status")`. There are also
   `PHASE_LAB_LOCATE_TOOLS`, `PHASE_CLASSIC_LOCATE_TOOLS` (opt-in via
   `CTX_MCP_EXPERIMENT=lab|classic`), and `LEGACY_LOCATE_TOOLS` (rich
   surfaces like `search`, `files`, `read`, `recall`, `neighbors`, `graph`,
   `outline`).
   `locate_tool_names(profile="locate"|"all")` returns
   `PHASE_LOCATE_TOOLS` for `"locate"`, or
   `PHASE_LOCATE_TOOLS + LEGACY_LOCATE_TOOLS` for `"all"`.

4. **Enriching the mcpServers entry:**
   `enrich_server_entry_permissions(entry, tool_slug, profile="locate")`:
   - Looks up `tool_permission_plan(tool_slug)` → a `ToolPermissionPlan`
     (`mechanism`, `sidecar_paths`, `notes`) from the `_TOOL_PLANS` dict.
   - If `mechanism` is `"already_builtin"` or `"docs_only"`, returns the
     entry unchanged (Copilot CLI already ships `tools:["*"]`; Codex/Zed/Amp
     have no embeddable field).
   - If `mechanism == "embedded_mcp"` (or `tool_slug` is in
     `_EMBEDDED_MCP_SLUGS` — includes **`kiro`**, `cline`, `roo-code`,
     `cursor`, `devin-desktop`, `pi`, `claude-code`):
     - clears any sticky `disabled: True` (special-cased: for `cursor` it
       pops the key; for everyone else in this branch it force-sets
       `disabled = False`),
     - flips `enabled` back to `True` if it was `False`,
     - sets `entry["autoApprove"] = locate_tool_names(profile)` (or `["*"]`
       for profile `"all"`),
     - sets `entry["alwaysAllow"]` to the same list.
   - If `tool_slug == "opencode"`, sets `autoApprove` similarly plus
     `enabled = True`.
   - Otherwise returns entry unchanged.
   This is the **direct embedded autoApprove/alwaysAllow mechanism** used by
   Cline/Roo/Cursor/Kiro/Devin/Pi/Claude Code/OpenCode server blocks.

5. **Cross-host permission "plans" table:** `_TOOL_PLANS: dict[str, ToolPermissionPlan]`
   in `mcp_permissions.py` maps slug → mechanism:
   - `cursor` → `sidecar_json`, path `.cursor/permissions.json` (Run Mode
     `mcpAllowlist` **plus** embedded autoApprove — belongs to both
     `_EMBEDDED_MCP_SLUGS` and has a sidecar plan; `enrich_server_entry_permissions`
     still special-cases `cursor` to `pop("disabled")` instead of forcing
     `False`).
   - `claude-code` → `sidecar_json`, path `.claude/settings.json`.
   - `codex` → `docs_only`, `.codex/SCUBIEE_MCP_PERMISSIONS.md`.
   - `copilot` → `already_builtin` (VS Code UI or `tools:["*"]`).
   - `continue` → `sidecar_yaml`, `.continue/scubiee-permissions.yaml` +
     `.continue/SCUBIEE_MCP_PERMISSIONS.md`.
   - `opencode` → `embedded_mcp`.
   - `zed` → `docs_only`, `.zed/SCUBIEE_MCP_PERMISSIONS.md`.
   - `amp` → `docs_only`, `.amp/SCUBIEE_MCP_PERMISSIONS.md`.
   - Loop at module load: `for _slug in _EMBEDDED_MCP_SLUGS:
     _TOOL_PLANS.setdefault(_slug, ToolPermissionPlan(mechanism="embedded_mcp", ...))`
     — this is what gives **`kiro`** (and `cline`, `roo-code`, `devin-desktop`,
     `pi`) their plan: pure embedded `autoApprove + alwaysAllow` on the
     `mcpServers.scubiee` entry, **no sidecar file at all**. So for Kiro the
     entire permission grant happens in step 4 (embedding), and
     `write_tool_permission_artifacts` short-circuits with
     `skipped=True, skip_reason="embedded on mcpServers entry during connect"`.

6. **Sidecar/project-level permission-surface writer:**
   `apply_permissions_to_repo_tool_surface(tool_slug, repo, profile, dry_run)`
   is a thin wrapper that calls `write_tool_permission_artifacts(...)`
   (same module). That function:
   - looks up the plan again; returns early (`skipped`) for `unknown tool`
     or `already_builtin`;
   - reads `CTX_MCP_PERMISSIONS_USER` env var to decide whether to also
     write a user-home copy (`include_user_home`);
   - branches on `tool_slug`:
     - **`cursor`**: `merge_cursor_permissions(root/".cursor/permissions.json", profile=...)`
       (project) and optionally `Path.home()/".cursor/permissions.json"` (user).
     - **`claude-code`**: `merge_claude_settings_permissions(root/".claude/settings.json", profile=...)`
       (project + optional user copy).
     - **`continue`**: writes `.continue/scubiee-permissions.yaml`
       (from `_continue_permissions_yaml`) + a README stub, via
       `atomic_write_text` (from `artifact_guard.py`).
     - **`codex` / `zed` / `amp`** (`docs_only`): writes a single markdown
       stub `SCUBIEE_MCP_PERMISSIONS.md` via `_permissions_readme(...)`.
     - **`embedded_mcp` plans** (e.g. Kiro, Cline, Roo, Cursor's embedded
       half, OpenCode): `report["skipped"] = True`,
       `report["skip_reason"] = "embedded on mcpServers entry during connect"`
       — nothing else to write; the grant already happened via
       `enrich_server_entry_permissions` in step 4.
   - Regardless of branch, always finishes by calling
     `_write_permissions_manifest(root, tool_slug, report, dry_run)`.

7. **Merge logic for the two concrete sidecar JSON formats:**
   - `merge_cursor_permissions(path, profile)`:
     - loads existing `.cursor/permissions.json` via `_load_json_object`
       (returns `{}` on missing/corrupt file — silently tolerant, unlike the
       mcp.json merge path which raises on corrupt JSON),
     - computes `additions = _cursor_mcp_allowlist(profile)` →
       for `profile="all"`: `["scubiee:*", "*:*"]`;
       for `profile="locate"`: `["scubiee:*"] + [f"*:{tool}" for tool in PHASE_LOCATE_TOOLS]`
       (the `*:{tool}` wildcards guard against Cursor renaming/prefixing the
       server namespace),
     - prunes stale classic/lab tool entries via
       `_prune_stale_scubiee_allowlist_entries` (drops leftover
       `*:focus`/`*:grep`/etc. from older connects when profile is `"locate"`),
     - merges into `document["mcpAllowlist"]` via `_merge_unique_strings`
       (order-preserving de-dup),
     - also rewrites `document["autoRun"]["allow_instructions"]`: strips any
       older "focus, grep, glob" coaching line and appends a fresh
       "Allow Scubiee MCP locate tools (gate, map, pack_context, ...)" line,
     - writes atomically via `_write_json_object` → `atomic_write_text`,
       `json.dumps(..., indent=2, sort_keys=True)`.
   - `merge_claude_settings_permissions(path, profile)`:
     - loads `.claude/settings.json`, sets `$schema` if absent,
     - reads/creates `document["permissions"]["allow"]` list,
     - prunes stale entries (same helper),
     - merges in `_claude_allow_rules(profile)` →
       for `"all"`: `["mcp__scubiee__*"]`;
       for `"locate"`: `[f"mcp__scubiee__{tool}" for tool in PHASE_LOCATE_TOOLS] + ["mcp__scubiee__*"]`
       (note: locate profile *also* appends the wildcard at the end —
       both explicit tool names and a trailing wildcard are present),
     - writes back via `_write_json_object`.

8. **Manifest / bookkeeping:** `_write_permissions_manifest(root, tool_slug, report, dry_run)`
   writes `.scubiee/mcp-permissions.json`, merging per-tool state:
   `{"tools": {slug: {"profile", "plan": ToolPermissionPlan.__dict__, "artifacts", "skipped"}}, "server": MCP_SERVER_NAME, "locate_tools": locate_tool_names()}`.
   This is a local audit trail, not something a host reads for approvals.

9. **mcp.json write-and-verify (the counterpart to permissions):**
   `_write_workspace_mcp` → `_write_mcp_json_keyed(path, key, entry)` merges
   the enriched `entry` (already containing autoApprove/alwaysAllow from
   step 4) into the correct top-level key (`mcpServers`, `servers`, `mcp`,
   or `amp.mcpServers` depending on host) under `_SERVER_NAME`, using
   `_load_json_for_merge` (raises `MCPConfigMergeError` on corrupt JSON or
   non-object root — stricter than the tolerant `_load_json_object` used for
   permission sidecars) and `strip_legacy_mcp_keys` (from `branding.py`) to
   remove old server aliases before re-inserting. After writing,
   `write_project_tool_surface` calls `mcp_install.py::verify_mcp_json(mcp_path)`
   on every written `.json` path and records failures into
   `report["mcp_verify"]`, flipping `report["ok"] = False` if any fail.

# Scubiee — MCP tool permission / allowlist install trace

## Problem restatement (≤8 lines)
Scubiee's `connect` command must write both an `mcpServers.scubiee` entry (command/args/env) AND
host-specific auto-approve state, so agents are never blocked by a host's "allow this tool?"
prompt. The tool list to auto-approve is centralized (`PHASE_LOCATE_TOOLS`), the enrichment of an
MCP server JSON block happens per host schema (`enrich_server_entry_permissions`), and separate
sidecar permission files (Cursor `permissions.json`, Claude `settings.json`, Continue YAML,
docs-only stubs) are merged non-destructively. `write_project_tool_surface` in
`rules_installer.py` is the per-repo, per-tool orchestrator that ties MCP-file write + GATE rules
+ sidecar permissions together; `install_tool` / `fan_out_tool_to_enrolled_repos` call it for every
enrolled repo on `scubiee connect`. A `"locate"` vs `"all"` `PermissionProfile` exists in the
permissions module, but only `"locate"` is ever passed from production call sites found.

## Ordered call/flow narrative

1. **Tool list defined** — `packages/pipeline/mcp_permissions.py::PHASE_LOCATE_TOOLS` (module-level
   tuple) is the canonical default-ship locate surface: `gate, map, pack_context, expand_context,
   collect_hot_context, workspace, expand, status`. `locate_tool_names(profile=...)` returns this
   list for `profile="locate"`, or this list **plus** `LEGACY_LOCATE_TOOLS` for `profile="all"`.
   Related lab/classic tool tuples (`PHASE_LAB_LOCATE_TOOLS`, `PHASE_CLASSIC_LOCATE_TOOLS`) are
   *not* auto-approved by default — only used to prune stale sticky grants.

2. **Per-host permission plan lookup** — `tool_permission_plan(slug)` looks up a
   `ToolPermissionPlan` (`slug`, `mechanism`, `sidecar_paths`, `notes`) from `_TOOL_PLANS` (a dict
   keyed by tool slug, seeded explicitly for cursor/claude-code/codex/copilot/continue/opencode/
   zed/amp, then defaulted for all `_EMBEDDED_MCP_SLUGS` — cline, roo-code, cursor, kiro,
   devin-desktop, pi, claude-code — to `mechanism="embedded_mcp"`).

3. **Enrich the `mcpServers.scubiee` entry** — `rules_installer.py::format_server_entry(tool, repo,
   pin_repo, schema)` builds the raw JSON/TOML/YAML server block (command/args/env per host
   schema: claude/vscode/opencode/amp/codex/continue/zed/copilot_cli), then calls
   `mcp_permissions.enrich_server_entry_permissions(entry, tool.slug, profile="locate")` before
   returning it. That function:
   - For `mechanism == "embedded_mcp"` (or slug in `_EMBEDDED_MCP_SLUGS`): clears any sticky
     `disabled: true` (special-cased `pop` for cursor, `= False` for others), sets `enabled=True`
     if it was `False`, and sets `entry["autoApprove"] = locate_tool_names(profile=...)` (or
     `["*"]` if profile is `"all"`), then mirrors it into `entry["alwaysAllow"]`.
   - For `opencode`: sets `autoApprove` similarly + `enabled=True`, drops `disabled`.
   - For `already_builtin` (Copilot CLI ships `tools:["*"]` already) and `docs_only` hosts
     (codex/zed/amp — no stable auto-approve JSON field): entry passed through unchanged.

4. **Sidecar / project-level permission surfaces written** —
   `mcp_permissions.write_tool_permission_artifacts(tool_slug, repo, profile, dry_run,
   include_user_home)` (aliased publicly as `apply_permissions_to_repo_tool_surface`) writes the
   host-specific sidecar file *in addition to* the embedded entry:
   - **cursor** → `merge_cursor_permissions(path)`: loads/merges `.cursor/permissions.json`,
     merges `mcpAllowlist` (adds `"scubiee:*"` plus `"*:<tool>"` per `PHASE_LOCATE_TOOLS` tool, or
     `["scubiee:*", "*:*"]` for `profile="all"`), prunes stale classic/lab entries
     (`_prune_stale_scubiee_allowlist_entries`), and appends an `autoRun.allow_instructions` line.
   - **claude-code** → `merge_claude_settings_permissions(path)`: merges `.claude/settings.json`
     `permissions.allow` list with `mcp__scubiee__<tool>` rules (`_claude_allow_rules`), plus a
     trailing `mcp__scubiee__*` wildcard, again pruning stale classic/lab rules.
   - **continue** → writes `.continue/scubiee-permissions.yaml` (an `allow: [Mcp(scubiee:<tool>)]`
     list the user must merge into `~/.continue/permissions.yaml`) + a README stub.
   - **codex / zed / amp** (`docs_only`) → writes a `SCUBIEE_MCP_PERMISSIONS.md` stub under each
     tool's dot-dir explaining there is no auto-approve file; user must approve via host UI.
   - **embedded_mcp hosts** (cline, roo-code, kiro, devin-desktop, pi) → **skipped** here
     (`report["skipped"]=True, skip_reason="embedded on mcpServers entry during connect"`) because
     step 3 already wrote `autoApprove`/`alwaysAllow` directly on the MCP JSON entry.
   - Every call also updates a manifest at `<repo>/.scubiee/mcp-permissions.json` recording which
     tools/profiles/artifacts were applied (`_write_permissions_manifest`).

5. **`write_project_tool_surface` ties MCP + rules + permissions together per repo/tool** —
   `rules_installer.py::write_project_tool_surface(repo, tool, dry_run)`:
   a. Resolves `enrolled = _is_enrolled(root)` (via `pipeline.mcp_locate._is_enrolled`).
   b. Calls `_write_workspace_mcp(tool, root)` → dispatches by `tool.slug` to write the correct
      project-local MCP file(s) (`.cursor/mcp.json`, `.kiro/settings/mcp.json`,
      `.vscode/mcp.json` + `.mcp.json` for copilot, `.cline/mcp.json`, `.roo/mcp.json`,
      `.codex/config.toml`, `.continue/mcpServers/scubiee.yaml`, `opencode.json`,
      `.amp/settings.json`, etc.) — each of these calls `format_server_entry(...)` internally,
      which is where step 3's `enrich_server_entry_permissions` already ran.
   c. Runs `verify_mcp_json` on each written `.json` path (checks bridge/worker command +
      `CTX_SCUBIEE_BUILD` env present) — failure flips `report["ok"]=False`.
   d. Calls `write_project_gate_rules(root, slugs=[tool.slug])` — writes the compact GATE/AGENTS
      rule text (separate concern from MCP permissions).
   e. Calls `mcp_permissions.apply_permissions_to_repo_tool_surface(tool.slug, root,
      dry_run=False)` — step 4's sidecar-file writer — and stores the result under
      `report["permissions"]`; a non-ok permissions report also flips `report["ok"]=False`.

6. **Fan-out across all hosts / all repos** —
   - `fan_out_tool_to_enrolled_repos(tool, remove=False, dry_run=False)` loops every managed repo
     (`_fan_out_managed_repos()` → `pipeline.managed_repos.managed_repo_paths(enrolled_only=False)`)
     and calls `write_project_tool_surface(repo, tool, dry_run)` for each.
   - `install_tool(tool, dry_run, repo)` (the actual `scubiee connect --<tool>` entry point) —
     removes legacy global MCP paths (`_remove_legacy_global_mcp`), then calls
     `fan_out_tool_to_enrolled_repos(tool, dry_run=False)`, aggregates errors, and finally records
     the tool as connected via `connect_state.add_connected_tool(tool.slug)`.
   - `apply_connected_tools_to_repo(repo, dry_run)` is the inverse direction — used by
     `scubiee init` / upgrade paths (`upgrade_scenarios.py`, `upgrade_supervisor.py`,
     `repo_lifecycle.py`) — loads `connect_state.load_connected_tools()` (globally connected
     slugs) and calls `write_project_tool_surface(root, tool, dry_run=False)` for each already
     connected tool against the one repo just enrolled/upgraded.
   - `pause_resume.py` calls `fan_out_tool_to_enrolled_repos(tool, remove=True, dry_run=False)` on
     stop, to strip the MCP surface (not the sidecar permission files) across all repos.

7. **Audit / doctor path** — `mcp_permissions.audit_permissions(repo)` reads
   `connect_state.load_connected_tools()`, then for each connected slug re-derives its
   `tool_permission_plan` and re-checks the actual on-disk state (Cursor `mcpAllowlist` prefix
   match, Claude `permissions.allow` prefix match, Continue yaml existence, or for
   `embedded_mcp`/`docs_only` hosts, reads the resolved project MCP JSON via
   `tool_registry.resolve_mcp_project_paths` and checks `autoApprove`/`alwaysAllow` is non-empty).
   Used by `scubiee doctor` to tell users to re-run `connect --<slug>` if permissions look stale.

## Path + symbol table

| # | Path | Symbol | Notes |
|---|------|--------|-------|
| 1 | `packages/pipeline/mcp_permissions.py` | `PHASE_LOCATE_TOOLS` (tuple, ~L29) | Canonical ship locate tool list |

## Problem restatement (≤8 lines)
Scubiee's `connect` command must write both an `mcpServers.scubiee` entry (command/args/env) AND
host-specific auto-approve state, so agents are never blocked by a host's "allow this tool?"
prompt. The tool list to auto-approve is centralized (`PHASE_LOCATE_TOOLS`), the enrichment of an
MCP server JSON block happens per host schema (`enrich_server_entry_permissions`), and separate
sidecar permission files (Cursor `permissions.json`, Claude `settings.json`, Continue YAML,
docs-only stubs) are merged non-destructively. `write_project_tool_surface` in
`rules_installer.py` is the per-repo, per-tool orchestrator that ties MCP-file write + GATE rules
+ sidecar permissions together; `install_tool` / `fan_out_tool_to_enrolled_repos` call it for every
enrolled repo on `scubiee connect`. A `"locate"` vs `"all"` `PermissionProfile` exists in the
permissions module, but only `"locate"` is ever passed from production call sites found.

## Ordered call/flow narrative

1. **Tool list defined** — `packages/pipeline/mcp_permissions.py::PHASE_LOCATE_TOOLS` (module-level
   tuple) is the canonical default-ship locate surface: `gate, map, pack_context, expand_context,
   collect_hot_context, workspace, expand, status`. `locate_tool_names(profile=...)` returns this
   list for `profile="locate"`, or this list **plus** `LEGACY_LOCATE_TOOLS` for `profile="all"`.
   Related lab/classic tool tuples (`PHASE_LAB_LOCATE_TOOLS`, `PHASE_CLASSIC_LOCATE_TOOLS`) are
   *not* auto-approved by default — only used to prune stale sticky grants.

2. **Per-host permission plan lookup** — `tool_permission_plan(slug)` looks up a
   `ToolPermissionPlan` (`slug`, `mechanism`, `sidecar_paths`, `notes`) from `_TOOL_PLANS` (a dict
   keyed by tool slug, seeded explicitly for cursor/claude-code/codex/copilot/continue/opencode/
   zed/amp, then defaulted for all `_EMBEDDED_MCP_SLUGS` — cline, roo-code, cursor, kiro,
   devin-desktop, pi, claude-code — to `mechanism="embedded_mcp"`).

3. **Enrich the `mcpServers.scubiee` entry** — `rules_installer.py::format_server_entry(tool, repo,
   pin_repo, schema)` builds the raw JSON/TOML/YAML server block (command/args/env per host
   schema: claude/vscode/opencode/amp/codex/continue/zed/copilot_cli), then calls

     `["*"]` if profile is `"all"`), then mirrors it into `entry["alwaysAllow"]`.

## Locate profile vs "all" (allow-all) — what actually differs

- The `PermissionProfile = Literal["locate", "all"]` type and `profile` kwarg thread through
  every function in `mcp_permissions.py` (`locate_tool_names`, `enrich_server_entry_permissions`,
  `_cursor_mcp_allowlist`, `_claude_allow_rules`, `_continue_permissions_yaml`,
  `write_tool_permission_artifacts`, `apply_permissions_to_repo_tool_surface`).
- `"locate"` (default everywhere): approve exactly `PHASE_LOCATE_TOOLS` (8 read-only tools);
  Cursor gets `scubiee:*` + one `*:<tool>` wildcard per tool; Claude gets one
  `mcp__scubiee__<tool>` rule per tool plus a trailing `mcp__scubiee__*`.
  `_prune_stale_scubiee_allowlist_entries` actively **removes** any lingering classic/lab tool
  grants (`focus`, `grep`, `glob`, `pinpoint`, `plate`, `pack_poly_embed`, `pack_semantic`,
  `map_context`) when profile is `"locate"` — a "sticky merge fix" for repos that were connected
  under an older classic/lab surface.
- `"all"`: Cursor allowlist collapses to `[f"{server}:*", "*:*"]` (full wildcard); Claude allow
  collapses to `[f"mcp__{server}__*"]`; embedded-MCP `autoApprove`/`alwaysAllow` becomes `["*"]`
  instead of the enumerated tool list; Continue YAML adds an extra `Mcp(scubiee:*)` line.
- **However**, grep across `rules_installer.py`, `mcp_install.py`, `mcp_restore.py`, `cli.py`, and
  the CLI entry points found **no production call site that passes `profile="all"`** — every real
  call (`format_server_entry` → `enrich_server_entry_permissions`, and the `write_project_tool_surface`
  → `apply_permissions_to_repo_tool_surface` chain) relies on the `"locate"` default. `"all"` is
  fully implemented but currently dormant/unreachable from `scubiee connect`, `init`, or `doctor`.
